direct_consumer_reviews.use_review: All five steps preserve the full compact embedded hypersurface claim and invariant Gaussian curvature. Local graph normals suffice; no global orientation is assumed. The graph-cover bridge and determinant formula retain Hessian nondegeneracy, finite compact amplitudes permit endpoint patch summation, and TT* gives restriction. The extension range uses the elementary Lq integration inequality; p=1 is separately obtained by direct Fourier bound, density and complex completeness.

Both steps use the earlier complete smooth graph bridge and graph curvature formula. A continuous normal is locally smooth with a locally constant sign, so nonzero curvature yields nonzero graph Hessian throughout each shrunk chart. Compact localization supplies finitely many supported weights. The corollary below uses this local construction without imposing the lemma’s optional global normal on its own Statement.

The six-step proof chooses compact K+ with invertible graph Hessian, isolates finitely many zeros near K for each fixed direction, and retains those zeros in enlarged balls for a parameter neighbourhood. Uniform gradient and inverse-Hessian bounds allow local stationary estimates, while add/subtract bumps handle a zero entering or leaving original amplitude support. A finite directional cover gives uniform constants. The general clause explicitly requires compact intrinsic support and uses the equivalent Gaussian curvature determinant, not a graph-only weakening.

Both steps use the graph tangent frame with positive Gram matrix G=I+grad h grad hT. Differentiated orthogonality gives <Snu Xj,Xk>=hjk/b and hence GA=D²h/b. The supplied Gram determinant b² yields det Snu=det D²h/b^(n+1); positive denominator proves both vanishing directions, including singular Hessian and n=2. Euclidean curvature equivalence is supplied by the fully read bridge.

The five steps bootstrap the earlier C1 inverse with the adjugate quotient derivative, then use a rank-one projection spectral basis for rigid graph coordinates. Transition chain rules and differentiated orthogonality prove all normal/shape interfaces, including standard Euclidean principal-curvature determinant. Finite ambient-ball bumps normalize by eta(B)/B only where B>0 and extend smoothly by zero; the empty compact set is treated explicitly.

current_manifest_entry.statement: For $n\ge2$, every smooth embedded hypersurface $S\subset\mathbb R^n$ is locally, after a rigid motion, the graph $X(y)=(y,h(y))$ of a $C^\infty$ function. The tangent, normal, shape operator and curvature of [[def-euclidean-hypersurface-normal-shape-operator-and-curvature]] are well defined and agree with their usual Euclidean hypersurface meanings. Every continuous unit normal on $S$ is locally smooth. Every compact $K\subset S$ admits finitely many graph pieces $S_j$ and nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_j$ on $S$, compactly supported in $S_j$, whose sum is one on a neighbourhood of $K$. If $S$ itself is compact, that sum is one everywhere.
